text:
mika: FYI canary run for raven-v4q (int4) is spiking JSON parse errors on the funcall suite, only on streaming path. dumping some examples and metrics below.

jordan: ugh, how bad is "parse error"? rate? any diffs vs fp16 or int8 canary? :thinking_face:

mika: parse_fail_rate jumped from 0.2% -> 3.8% on the int4 pool for the same workload. fp16 and int8 stable. affects 2 of 15 prompt templates we use.

ash: can you paste a raw broken output? might be footer/header noise or missing closing bracket from cutoff.

mika: sure — here's one raw streaming snippet we captured (exact chunk reassembly):

```
Assistant: Here is the analysis you asked for.
Response-ID: 9a7c
{
  "action": "create_issue",
  "args": {
    "title": "Investigate int4 funcall parse spike",
    "description": "observed when prompt includes long system note"
  }

```

mika: note the missing closing brace and an extra "Response-ID:" header on a separate line — our strict JSON parser fails fast.

sasha: ah ok, header got injected by our telemetry layer? we saw a response-id glue in the streaming middleware last week. but why only int4?

luis: my theory: int4 model triggers slightly different tokenization/stopprob leading to early EOS emission mid-json; combined with our prefix KV cache trimming the earlier array sentinel is lost. net effect: truncated JSON + stray middleware header in chunk ordering.

ash: can we reproduce with deterministic seeds? run the same prompt on devbox with int4 and log token offsets and chunk boundaries.

mika: ran a few deterministic attempts — repro is flaky but possible with batch_size=3 and kv_cache_prefix_trim=true. attaching short log snippet: 

```
[stream-chunk 0] "{\n  \"action\": \"create_issue\",\n  \"args\": {\n    \"title\": \"...\""
[stream-chunk 1] "\n  }\n"
[stream-chunk 2] "Response-ID: 9a7c\n\n"
```

eva: that ordering would definitely break a naive reassembly+strict-parse. we should make the reassembler ignore top-of-stream headers and run a final whitespace-trim before JSON parse. also consider a tolerant fallback that attempts to repair (wrap in [] or append missing brace) before sending to toolchain.

jordan: repair heuristics are risky — we need to measure false positives. can we instead add a simple pre-parse sanitizer: remove lines matching /^Response-ID:/ and drop leading/trailing non-json bytes until first "{" and last "}"?

mika: implemented a prototype sanitizer and rerun: parse_fail_rate dropped to 0.9% on the canary. still higher than baseline but much better.

luis: long-term we should fix source: either ensure the middleware headers are emitted as structured metadata (not inline), or ensure the model doesn't emit those tokens. but middleware change is safer.

sasha: for rollout plan: 1) enable pre-parse sanitizer in canary path for int4 only (A), 2) run 24h canary with token-offset tracing (B), 3) if <1% failures and no false-positive repairs, promote sanitizer to all int variants (C).

mika: +1. also propose adding a strict-vs-tolerant metric in the eval harness so we can track how many repairs were applied vs successful.

deploy-bot: will schedule canary config update at 03:00 UTC — will post deploy status.

ash: one more datapoint — observed that streaming responses with function call arrays (large arrays) are more sensitive. maybe the streaming buffer boundary coincides with array end. consider emitting a small sentinel token pair before JSON starts like "<<JSON>>" and strip it in sanitizer.

jordan: sentinel helps but changes model output; prefer middleware header move. however sentinel as a temporary workaround for on-prem/private deployments is ok.

mika: okay timeline: sanitizer + header-ignore enabled in canary tonight, token-offset logging on for the next 48h. i'll post a short summary / metrics snapshot mid-run. thanks all :thumbsup:

luis: if sanitizer looks good we should bake into the SDK parse helper so customers see fewer parse errors out of the box.

sasha: filing follow-ups: infra ticket to remove inline Response-ID emission (INF-523), SDK ticket for parse-helper (SDK-784).

mika: posted INF-523 and SDK-784 links in thread.

eva: small note — add a test in our eval suite comparing repaired vs original outputs for semantic equality to make sure repairs don't change intent.

mika: good call. adding to SDK-784.

jordan: cool. ping me if you need any more logs or reproducer scripts.

mika: will do. end of thread for now.
